scope: Theorem 5.1 (Ostrovsky–Rabani, normalized form) of the manuscript “Edit Distance in l1: Matching Bounds up to Constants in the Exponent” (preprints/Edit-Distance-in-l1-Matching-Bounds-up-to-Constants-in-the-Exponent-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 099 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c554cfee6ede3e18), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an absolute constant C0 such that, for every integer m ≥ 3, there is a map gm : {0, 1}m → ℓ1 satisfying ED(u, v) ≤ ∥gm(u) − gm(v)∥1 ≤ Dm ED(u, v), Dm = exp C0 p log m log log m  . (5.1) Here ED permits unit-cost substitutions as well as insertions and deletions.
